title: fix(scripts): the polarity census pairs a key with the schema its own clause declares (objectui#9754 slice 2)
body:
Part of objectui#9754 — **slice 2, WINDOW PAIRING**. ⛔ This does not close that card: the limits list is explicitly not a closed count, and two further sources are named in it here without being repaired. objectui#9754 remains open.

Clause-②: no — 内部普查脚本的精度,无公开导出、无作者面

Merge base: `592402ea33` (computed on this branch, not inherited). Head this report is written at: `0357514f24`.

## What moved

`scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs` paired **every schema symbol a SENTENCE names** with **every key that sentence names**. That is the cartesian product over a window nothing chose, and the instrument names the cost on itself, verbatim, under *"The limits that produce this instrument's false positives"*:

> WINDOW PAIRING. A sentence may name schema S and key K and predicate K of something else entirely — a registry-local type, another node, a spec schema. V pairs them because they share a sentence. This is the limit the card's own author stated first, and it is still the largest source.

⭐ In one line, and bounded to what I controlled: **I stopped pairing a key with a schema when the key is predicated of something else** — of a registry-local type, of another node, of a zod method, of a CLI subcommand, of a DOM tag. ⛔ No claim is made here about what the census reports on any tree after this merges.

The window is now the **declaration clause**, and the pairing is made **once per occurrence**. The rule has five cases and they are on `readWindow`, not restated here:

1. the clause the key is written in, when that clause declares;
2. else the clause immediately before it, when that one declares — the coordinated object list, `` `S` declares `a` and no `b` ``;
3. else, when no declaration clause precedes the key anywhere in the sentence, the sentence's first declaration clause — the same fallback the cross-sentence pronoun already takes, and the FIRST clause only;
4. else **none** — a declaration clause does precede it, but another predication was opened in between, and reaching back across that is the pairing this refuses;
5. a relative or parenthetical clause has no subject of its own, so it takes its antecedent's — `` `S` (which declares `k`) ``, `` `S`, whose face declares `k` ``.

Two residues earlier slices handed here are dealt with:

- **POLARITY BY CLAUSE's residue** — *"a sentence whose SAME key sits in two declaration clauses of opposite polarity resolves to the first one, because choosing between them is the WINDOW PAIRING question below"* — is **closed**. It is not closed by choosing: the sentence used to hold one reading per key and now holds one per occurrence, so each claim is judged against the schema ITS OWN clause names.
- **objectui#9767's residue** — *"`PRESENT_DECLARATION` still reads the restored clause … That is a population question, not a polarity one"* — is **not** taken here, deliberately: it moves the population, and this change moves only the verdict (every population counter is byte-identical, see below). It stays named in the limits list.

## ⚠️ This narrows what the instrument flags, so the risk is the mirror of the usual one

The whole before/after flag set, **key by key**, adjudicated row by row, is in the `os-dev-report` comment on objectui#9754. The summary of the adjudication:

- Every dropped row was read against its sentence and, where the reading turned on it, against the tree. **Every one is a false positive.** ⛔ No true positive is lost.
- One row I first lost — a live contradiction about a key inherited from `BaseSchema` — is what rule 5 exists for. I measured the loss, wrote rule 5, and measured it back. It is flagged on this branch.
- Three of the dropped rows turn out to be false positives of the **member index's own reach** rather than of the window (a `z.lazy` face the index reads as empty; a face whose heritage clause is an `Omit` of a `Partial` of a spec type, across a package boundary). They are correctly dropped and for a reason this slice did not fix — said here rather than counted as a win.

Three legs refuse the "precision bought with blindness" purchase, and each is pinned and ablated:

| leg | what it refuses |
|---|---|
| a key the clause DOES predicate of the named schema still flags | trading false positives for false negatives |
| a coordinated object list past the cut still reaches its declaration clause | narrowing to the clause the key SITS in |
| the pinned blind spot (the cross-sentence pronoun, four keys) still reads | the standing acceptance condition on this reader |

**The population is untouched.** `entriesScanned`, `sentencesScanned`, `matchedAssertions`, `matchedQuoted`, `matchedEntries`, `pronounResolved`, `pastOnlySentences`, `litControlEntries` and the whole `unresolvedSchemas` bucket (objectui#9767's two lines) are identical before and after, on the same corpus at the same ref. This change moves the verdict only.

## Ablation — three legs, each proved on disk

⛔ Not the editor's exit code. Each leg: HEAD blob hash read first, anchor counted before and after, a **textually distinct** marker counted before and after, disk hash compared, restore under a `trap` and proved by `git diff HEAD` being empty.

| ablation | anchor→marker | pin-12 rows that went red |
|---|---|---|
| the clause window (`schemasOf(gov)` → the sentence's schemas) | 1→0 / 0→1, blob `69b7b9e7…` → `3dfd88bb…` | "stops pairing", "did NOT buy it with blindness", "two declaration clauses" |
| the relative opener (regex → one that never matches) | 1→0 / 0→1, blob `69b7b9e7…` → `b7247c0b…` | "a relative clause reaches its antecedent" |
| the coordinated list (rule 2 disabled) | 1→0 / 0→1, blob `69b7b9e7…` → `ff19c75e…` | "coordinated object list", "a relative clause reaches its antecedent" |

All three restored to `69b7b9e7…` with `git diff HEAD` empty.

⚠️ **One row refused my reading and it is reported rather than retried away.** I predicted the coordinated-list row would go red under the sentence-window ablation. It stayed **green**, and the reason is correct rather than weak: that fixture sentence names ONE schema, so the sentence window and the clause window coincide on it and only the coordination leg can move it. The pin's prose now says that, and the docblock records which leg holds each row — measured, not assumed.

## A further false-positive source, added to the list rather than repaired

The limits list refuses to be counted and says so: *"the list is THE LIST, and is not a closed count: ⛔ read nothing into its length, and add to it here when you find another."* ⇒ I added one:

**A TABLE OF SUPERSEDED READINGS.** An entry may carry a table whose first column is a reading it is **retiring** and whose later columns are what falsified it and when. Every cell of a row is joined into one sentence (deliberately — a table row is not a paragraph), so the retired claim reads as a present-tense assertion in ASSERTION position while its correction sits beside it, unread. Quotation position does not reach it: the retired reading is not quoted, it is tabulated.

- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `pnpm check:changeset-claims`, `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`, `pnpm check:new-line-citations`, `pnpm check:entry-guard` — all exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the four changed paths — NOT GOVERNED.
- Exit codes were captured before any pipe, per this lane's instrument traps.

## ⛔ Fences honoured

⛔ No changeset body is touched and no flagged entry is swept — adjudication precedes touching, and ROTTED and BORN FALSE take opposite repairs. `.changeset/5632-…` belongs to objectui#9753 and is read here only as evidence, never edited. ⛔ No cardinal is carried into the card, the changeset or the instrument's header; every reading in this PR was taken fresh at the merge base above and none is inherited from objectui#9727, objectui#9765 or this card's body.
